questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Laplace Transform of the Derivative of a Function
questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ for $s>4$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous over $[0,\infty ),$ $f(0)=6,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{6s-10}{{s}^{2}-2s-8},\,s>4.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
L{{f}^{′}(t)}=sL{f(t)}-f(0).
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{′}(t)} & =sL{f(t)}-f(0) \\  & =s\cdot \frac{6s-10}{{s}^{2}-2s-8}-6 \\  & =\frac{s(6s-10)-6({s}^{2}-2s-8)}{{s}^{2}-2s-8} \\  & =\frac{2s+48}{{s}^{2}-2s-8}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>4.$

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ for $s>3$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous over $[0,\infty ),$ $f(0)=2,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{2s-3}{{s}^{2}-3s},\,s>3.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
L{{f}^{′}(t)}=sL{f(t)}-f(0).
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{′}(t)} & =sL{f(t)}-f(0) \\  & =s\cdot \frac{2s-3}{{s}^{2}-3s}-2 \\  & =\frac{s(2s-3)-2({s}^{2}-3s)}{{s}^{2}-3s} \\  & =\frac{3s}{s(s-3)} \\  & =\frac{3}{s-3}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>3.$

questions.worked_solution:

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ for $s>1$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous over $[0,\infty ),$ $f(0)=5,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{5s-4}{{s}^{2}-s},\,s>1.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
L{{f}^{′}(t)}=sL{f(t)}-f(0).
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{′}(t)} & =sL{f(t)}-f(0) \\  & =s\cdot \frac{5s-4}{{s}^{2}-s}-5 \\  & =s\cdot \frac{5s-4}{s(s-1)}-5 \\  & =\frac{5s-4}{s-1}-5 \\  & =\frac{1}{s-1}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>1.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Laplace Transform of the Second Derivative of a Function
questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform $L{{f}^{″}(t)}$ for $s>3,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ ${f}^{′}(0)=4,$ $f(0)=2,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{2s-4}{{s}^{2}-4s+3},\,s>3.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{″}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{2s-4}{{s}^{2}-4s+3}-s\cdot 2-4 \\  & =\frac{2{s}^{2}(s-2)}{{s}^{2}-4s+3}-2(s+2) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{s}^{2}(s-2)-({s}^{2}-4s+3)(s+2)}{{s}^{2}-4s+3} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{({s}^{3}-2{s}^{2})-({s}^{3}-2{s}^{2}-5s+6)}{{s}^{2}-4s+3} \\  & =\frac{10s-12}{{s}^{2}-4s+3}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>3.$

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform $L{{f}^{″}(t)}$ for $s>1,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ ${f}^{′}(0)=-1,$ $f(0)=2,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{2s+1}{{s}^{2}+s-2},\,s>1.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{″}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{2s+1}{{s}^{2}+s-2}-s\cdot 2-(-1) \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}(2s+1)}{{s}^{2}+s-2}-(2s-1) \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}(2s+1)-({s}^{2}+s-2)(2s-1)}{{s}^{2}+s-2} \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}(2s+1)-{s}^{2}(2s-1)-(s-2)(2s-1)}{{s}^{2}+s-2} \\  & =\frac{2{s}^{2}-(2{s}^{2}-5s+2)}{{s}^{2}+s-2} \\  & =\frac{5s-2}{{s}^{2}+s-2}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>1.$

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform $L{{f}^{″}(t)}$ for $s>1,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ ${f}^{′}(0)=-1,$ $f(0)=0,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{1}{s-{s}^{2}},\,s>1.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{″}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{s-{s}^{2}}-s\cdot (0)-(-1) \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}}{s(1-s)}+1 \\  & =\frac{s}{1-s}+1 \\  & =\frac{s+1-s}{1-s} \\  & =\frac{1}{1-s}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>1.$

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform $L{{f}^{″}(t)}$ for $s>0,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ ${f}^{′}(0)=0,$ $f(0)=2,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{2{s}^{2}+1}{s({s}^{2}+1)},\,s>0.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{″}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{2{s}^{2}+1}{s({s}^{2}+1)}-s\cdot 2-0 \\  & =\frac{s(2{s}^{2}+1)}{{s}^{2}+1}-2s \\  & =\frac{2{s}^{3}+s-2{s}^{3}-2s}{{s}^{2}+1} \\  & =-\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>0.$

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform $L{{f}^{″}(t)}$ for $s>1,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ ${f}^{′}(0)=0,$ $f(0)=1,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{{s}^{2}-s+1}{{s}^{3}-{s}^{2}},\,s>1.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{″}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{{s}^{2}-s+1}{{s}^{3}-{s}^{2}}-s\cdot (1)-0 \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}({s}^{2}-s+1)}{{s}^{2}(s-1)}-s \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}-s+1}{s-1}-s \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}-s+1-{s}^{2}+s}{s-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{s-1}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>1.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Laplace Transform of the Derivative of a Function
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of $f'(t)$ for $s > 3$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous over $[0,\infty),$ $f(0)=0,$ and

$$
\mathcal{L}\left\{f(t)\right\} =  \dfrac{6}{s^2-5s+6}, \quad s>3.
$$

Assume that $f'$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s) = \mathcal L \{f(t)\}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty).$ If $f'(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty),$ then

$$
\mathcal{L}\left\{ f'(t) \right\}  = s \mathcal{L}\left\{  f(t)  \right\} -  f(0).
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of $f'(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{′}(t)} & =sL{f(t)}-f(0) \\  & =s\cdot \frac{6}{{s}^{2}-5s+6}-0 \\  & =\frac{6s}{{s}^{2}-5s+6}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s > 3.$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the Laplace transform $\mathcal{L}\left\{f''(t) \right\}$ for $s > 0,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty),$ $f'(0)=2,$ $f(0)=-1,$ and

$$
\mathcal{L}\left\{f(t)\right\} =   \dfrac{2 - s}{s^2+4}, \quad s>0.
$$

Assume that $f'$ is continuous and $f''$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s) = \mathcal L \{f(t)\}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty).$ If $f'(t)$ is continuous and $f''(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of $f''(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0) \\  & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{2-s}{{s}^{2}+4}-s\cdot (-1)-2 \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}(2-s)}{{s}^{2}+4}+s-2 \\  & =-\frac{{s}^{2}(s-2)}{{s}^{2}+4}+(s-2) \\  & =(s-2)(-\frac{{s}^{2}}{{s}^{2}+4}+1) \\  & =(s-2)(\frac{4}{{s}^{2}+4}) \\  & =\frac{4(s-2)}{{s}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s > 0.$
